claim_review: Individually authored from corresponding source facts and original photographs reviewed in this task. Structure, closure, lining and paired-size differences are model-specific. Numeric size labels use owner-confirmed EU convention; paired labels remain intact. Current selector choices and MOQ are labelled as listed, not physical stock. No unsupported chemistry, tested performance, certification, weight or unconfirmed stock. Only highlights and FAQ.
highlights: Oxford-fabric lace-up casual shoes with a defined toe surround and rubber sole. The low collar and continuous lace panel retain a straightforward everyday shape. Black, Tan and Dark Brown offer neutral choices through EU 36–48.

faq.question: Which color and EU size choices are listed?
faq.answers: DarkBrown: EU 36–48; Tan: EU 36–48; Black: EU 36–48.

faq.question: What upper and sole construction is specified?
faq.answers: Oxford-fabric upper and rubber outsole, with a conventional lace-up front and low collar. Compare the toe surround and heel detailing in the full color photo.

faq.question: What should I assess on a sample?
faq.answers: Adjust the laces with the intended socks, then check toe room, instep fit and heel hold before choosing the bulk EU size mix.

faq.question: What is the minimum order for the original style?
faq.answers: The listed original-style minimum is 2 pairs. Quantity pricing is shown on this page; logo and custom packaging proposals are quoted separately.

faq.question: How can I request a sample?
faq.answers: Send the selected color or lining option, EU size and delivery postcode for a sample quotation covering the pair, courier charge and proposed dispatch date.

faq.question: What should I send for logo or packaging requirements?
faq.answers: Send the logo artwork, preferred placement, packaging brief and order quantity. The proposal for this style will set out the applicable minimum, cost and sample process.

faq.question: How can I get a delivered quotation?
faq.answers: Send pair quantities by color and EU size, the destination postcode or port and the packaging request. The quotation separates product cost and freight and includes the proposed dispatch and transit schedule.
